title: Jason Calacanis: How to angel invest by betting on founders, starting small, and being relentlessly helpful
summary: Jason Calacanis explains why he moved from "I only invest in myself" to angel investing, and walks through the playbook in his book Angel. Bet on the founder rather than the idea, start with small checks across many deals, and be psychotically helpful. Insist on monthly updates, and wait for a launched product before writing a check.

principles.text: Judge the founder, not the idea. Your own read on whether an idea works is limited, so double down on whether the person will succeed.
principles.quote: that really is the secret to being a great investor it's just removing your ability to know if this Pro idea is going to work and doubling down on your ability to know if the person is going to succeed

principles.text: Don't dwell on why a startup will fail. List the one or two reasons it could work and weigh those.
principles.quote: when I look at startups now I don't look at all the reasons of why it will fail I'll write them down sometimes uh and then I usually rip that page up and then I just list the one or two reasons of why it will work

principles.text: Start with many small checks but act as if each were big. You gain experience, a network and a reputation as helpful.
principles.quote: your first 10 investment should just be $1,000 into you know a random number of syndicates on Angel list or on seed invest but act as if you put in 10,000 or 100,000

principles.text: Wait until a startup has launched with a few real customers before investing. This filters out most failures.
principles.quote: if you invest in only launch products you've already eliminated 97% of the failures

principles.text: Get monthly updates from founders, including ones you passed on. Silence from a portfolio company usually signals failure.
principles.quote: if you're not getting those updates it's a 99% chance the company's going out of business

principles.text: Great founders have a maniacal, unnecessary attention to detail and craftsmanship, even if they are annoying to deal with.
principles.quote: that maniacal sense of detail that most people don't see that's what greatness is about is an intention to detail that's unnecessary right and the great Founders all have that
